candidates.speaker: Daniel Dennett
candidates.proposition: The distinction between deterministic chaos and quantum indeterminacy makes no moral difference and is not a cheap substitute for allegedly real randomness.
candidates.attributionBasis: The turn begins with an explicit statement of disagreement and continues uninterrupted until Harris answers the moral-difference claim.
candidates.loadBearingReason: The claim directly supports compatibilism by denying that metaphysical indeterminacy supplies any morally relevant freedom unavailable in a deterministic world.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Harris's characterization of coin-flip randomness as merely a surrogate for true randomness and of prediction as threatening authorship.

candidates.contextSummary: After Harris argues that complete advance prediction would produce a marionette-like loss of authorship, Dennett disputes the implied downgrade of deterministic randomness.

candidates.speaker: Sam Harris
candidates.proposition: The contrast between deterministic chaos and quantum indeterminacy was offered only as a distinction between physical facts, not as a source of moral difference.
candidates.attributionBasis: Harris directly corrects Dennett's characterization in a short, uninterrupted clarification before Dennett resumes.
candidates.loadBearingReason: The clarification preserves Harris's argument from being treated as dependent on quantum indeterminacy having special moral significance.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Dennett's response that deterministic chaos and quantum indeterminacy make no moral difference.

candidates.contextSummary: Dennett has just argued that the two physical regimes are morally equivalent; Harris narrows his prior point to a physical distinction alone.

candidates.speaker: Daniel Dennett
candidates.proposition: People are mistaken to think they need libertarian free will because the forms of free will worth wanting are fully compatible with determinism.
candidates.attributionBasis: Dennett develops the point in a continuous turn that ends immediately before Harris explicitly states agreement.
candidates.loadBearingReason: This is the compatibilist thesis at the center of the motion: worthwhile human freedom does not require exemption from deterministic causation.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Harris's insistence that the libertarian sense of authorship is psychologically important even though people lack that freedom.

candidates.contextSummary: Following agreement that quantum indeterminacy adds no moral difference, Dennett concludes that libertarian expectations are delusive and unnecessary.
